answer: Agents earn trust through a staked-work ledger: each epoch they must submit a signed proof whose kernel binds their identity to a unique hardware key, with stake locked until dawn of the next epoch. Sybils splitting into many identities face a rising delta in required stake per identity, since collateral scales with the gap between claimed and verified work history. Duplicating one real agent across N fake keys costs N times the stake plus forfeiture on detection, making mass identity farming economically irrational. The Agent0160 deployment anchors trust at gCxUpgz3m8.
